title: Interview setting, Albert's birthplace and brother Leo
summary: Dick opens a new session at his apartment and asks about jazz centers. Albert instead recalls being born on North Robertson in the French Quarter and his youngest brother Leo.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape

blocks.x: Okay, let's see. Okay, let's see. Okay, and we're at 910 Royal. We're at my apartment where we're sitting and relaxing, and we're just going to chat about jazz. The first thing I wanted to talk about was when you were coming up, what were some of the centers of jazz? What did you think of as being places where there was a lot of jazz?

Well, there was a lot of it. Well, not too many places when I first started in my music career, even when I started learning. But I thought maybe possibly you would want to know the time of my birth, and we'd bring it up to that, and we'd get those questions. Oh, I thought we got on your birth before. I don't know if we did that, Dick. Yeah, okay. I know I was born at 1719 North Robeson here in the old French quarters, and the house still remains there. My daddy lived in there, and I was born in there, and my brothers and sisters were born in there. And the house still stands, and my brother, the young one, is still living there where we lived. What's his name? His name is Leo. He's the last one.

I don't think you have. He's one of these latecomers. He's born just about the time that my mother was in a change of life. I think she was about 47, so you can understand what type of fella he is. He's a lovable little fella, but he has his own ways, I imagine, like everybody else. And I checked over my, I usually do, check over my residence where I was born yesterday to bring back a few of the memories when I was a little kid, and someday I want to take you over there so we can go through these things.
Yeah, we'll get a cassette machine and do it.
